01_lightning-strikes-man-survives-2026.j.script: A man got struck by lightning and somehow walked away alive. He was crossing a parking lot when a bolt hit nearby and the current jumped through him, throwing him to the ground. Lightning carries up to a billion volts and is five times hotter than the surface of the sun, yet most people who are struck actually survive, because the charge flashes over the skin instead of stopping the heart. He walked away with burns shaped like branching lines across his back, called a lightning flower. Doctors say the fact that it was raining may have saved him. So why do some people survive a direct hit?

It looked harmless, almost funny, until the Corolla Wild Horse Fund got the call: apples can kill their wild horses, causing choking and deadly colic if the herd finds them first. Local families, deputies, and volunteer turtle patrols dropped everything and raced the clock, bagging up the fruit handful by handful before the horses could. 05_venezuela-earthquake-rescue-2026.json.title: Buried for 8 Days. He Walked Out Alive.
05_venezuela-earthquake-rescue-2026.json.script: Buried Alive For Eight Days? When Venezuela's twin earthquakes leveled a shopping mall in La Guaira, the whole parking structure came down — except one thing: a tiny security booth, and the guard still inside it. Hernan Gil Flores spent eight days trapped in that pocket of space while 29 feet of concrete crushed everything around him. Rescuers lowered water and nutrients down a narrow shaft just to keep him alive, talking to him through a telescopic camera while international crews from Chile, Costa Rica, the U.S., Portugal, and Mexico spent three straight days tunneling toward him. On day eight, they pulled him out alive, in what officials called a miracle. More than 2,300 people didn't make it. So what are the odds a security booth saves your life?
